title: Microsoft is adding "hybrid intelligence" to Windows, so apps can choose between local and cloud AI models.
key_facts: Microsoft calls the plan "hybrid intelligence", built on its HydraFusion model router.
Windows apps and Copilot features will use local models when it makes sense and cloud models when it does not.
Local agents run in Microsoft's Execution Containers (MXCs), sandboxes with permissions applied at runtime.
Microsoft is extending Windows ML support to llama.cpp, a local AI inference engine.
The feature rolls out to GitHub Copilot next week and to the Copilot app over the next few months.
The Register doubts the effect on battery life, fan noise and workload quality of running models locally.
quote_evidence: Built atop Microsoft's HydraFusion model router, Windows apps and Copilot features will soon be able to use local models when it makes sense and cloud-based models when it doesn't.
Microsoft is rolling out its hybrid intelligence functionality to GitHub Copilot - its AI code assistant - next week and its Copilot app over the next few months.
why_it_matters_hint: Local and private AI on Windows PCs changes what users' data leaves the machine, but most features are announced rather than live.
